p5_b1.ocr: The following table presents a comprehensive analysis of the efficacy of various activities conducted to manage tick populations, specifically focusing on the species Rhipicephalus sanguineus and Ixodes ricinus. The study monitored these tick species over a designated period, categorized by distinct Study Day or Week intervals. Each interval allows for a systematic evaluation of the impact of specific interventions on tick reduction, providing valuable insights into their effectiveness. In the context of this research, 50 R. sanguineus ticks (comprising 25 males and 25 females) and 40 I.

p5_b2.ocr: ricinus ticks (20 males and 20 females) were subjected to various control measures. The Activity column outlines the specific interventions implemented during the study, while the efficacy (%) column quantifies the percentage reduction in tick populations attributable to each activity. This structured approach not only facilitates the comparison of different interventions but also aids in identifying the most effective strategies for tick management. By analyzing the data, stakeholders can make informed decisions regarding the adoption of targeted pest control measures to mitigate the risks associated with tick-borne diseases, thereby enhancing public health outcomes.
